subject.title: Durable Core PR 3/6: add owner-first Gateway recovery

question: Should OpenClaw adopt an opt-in shared durable runtime as a core product boundary, including persistent wake coordination and fail-closed Gateway authority mode, or require owner-specific recovery improvements instead?
rationale: The patch is a coherent implementation of a proposed architecture, but neither the open RFC nor the open storage predecessor establishes maintainer acceptance of a permanent cross-owner persistence and operator-facing configuration contract.

options.title: Pause for a core boundary decision
options.body: Keep this PR and the stack open without merge automation until maintainers explicitly sponsor or reject the shared durable-runtime contract.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow v1 contract
options.body: Accept the owner-first durable layer only with documented authority-mode startup behavior, ownership limits, and upgrade/Doctor support expectations.

options.title: Prefer owner-specific recovery work
options.body: Reject the shared control plane and split any proven silence or restart gaps into task, flow, subagent, or session-owner repairs.

recommendation.title: Pause for a core boundary decision
recommendation.body: Keep this PR and the stack open without merge automation until maintainers explicitly sponsor or reject the shared durable-runtime contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor is the declared implementation owner and best available contact to clarify or narrow the proposed series; final product acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
